accuracy_stats.method: 95% Wilson score interval per model; exact McNemar test per pair on the flows both models answered (only the flows where exactly one was right count), Holm-corrected across pairs. An unreadable answer counts as wrong.

pairs.verdict: no evidence of a real difference (could be chance on these flows)

misclass_cost.note: RESOURCE cost when a model is right (correct = TP/TN) vs wrong (incorrect = FP/FN). Cost comparison only — not an analysis of why models misclassify or which detects better.

advanced.note: Read-only analytical expansion computed from the existing locked run data (no re-runs). Resource/measurement framing only. TTFT is the per-agent time-to-first-token (prefill proxy); decode = wall_time_s - ttft_s. VRAM elsewhere is marginal working memory. misclass_cost compares RESOURCE COST when right vs wrong — it does not analyse or rank why models misclassify.

pareto.note: Accuracy (higher better) vs mean latency / mean tokens (lower better). pareto_latency / pareto_tokens flag the non-dominated models on each front.

notes.failures: empty_output = 0 output tokens; hit_token_cap = output reached the agent's max_new_tokens (likely truncated); unparseable_label = the label agent's reply matched no allowed label. The pipeline has no timeouts or retries by design (one call per agent), so timeouts are not applicable and retries are always 0.
notes.latency: Per-agent latency = the agent's own model call (perf_counter); shares are of the summed agent time, which is the flow's end-to-end latency.
notes.overhead: Agentic overhead = tokens of earlier agents' outputs re-sent in later prompts (hand-offs: reason <- perceive, decide <- reason+perceive, act <- reason). Estimated from the recorded output-token counts; the rest of the input (system prompt, flow features, instructions) is the task input.
notes.timeline: Agents run back-to-back; a flow's timeline is the cumulative sum of its agents' recorded call times (framework overhead between calls is not part of the measurement).
notes.vram: Per-agent peak working VRAM = torch allocator peak above the pre-call baseline (excludes the loaded weights); null on CPU/mock.

cold_start.note: Load time = loading the weights onto the GPU in a fresh worker (after any first-use download, which is not counted). First-flow penalty = first flow minus the median of the rest.

more_resource_efficient.basis: efficiency-only SAW composite (latency, VRAM, tokens; accuracy excluded)

comparison.statement: More resource-efficient (efficiency-only SAW): tie (within 0.5 points); validity check, answers matching the reference label: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 20.0%, meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct 20.0%.

notes.cost: Cost per 1,000 flows = mean end-to-end latency per flow x 1,000 / 3,600 x the GPU's hourly price. Pipeline time only (model loading excluded).
notes.energy: GPU board power sampled from the parent process (NVML, or nvidia-smi) while the workers ran, integrated over each model's window (first flow start -> last flow end, 1 s timestamp resolution) and divided by its flows. Whole-board power, including idle power between agent calls; model loading excluded. Sampling runs in a separate process from the measured worker, so it does not add to the measured latency.
notes.energy_net: Net of idle = the same energy minus the idle board power (mean of the samples taken for a few seconds right before the model's worker started, GPU idle) x the window length. The GPU can still be leaving a high-power state when the idle sample starts, so the net figure is a lower bound on the model's own energy share.
notes.energy_uncertainty: Uncertainty of energy per flow ≈ (sampling interval + 1 s timestamp resolution) ÷ the model's window: the power at the window's edges is not known exactly. It is small for long runs and large for short ones.

drivers.method: Spearman rank correlation of each model-visible flow feature with the flow's end-to-end latency and total tokens, per model (the 6 strongest for latency shown). Input scaling: a least-squares line of latency against the flow's input tokens (all agents). Correlation is not cause: features move together.

effect_sizes.method: Cliff's delta (P(A>B) - P(A<B); negative = Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct lower) with Romano et al. magnitude; percentile bootstrap 95% CI of mean(A) - mean(B), 2000 resamples, seed 46. The Kruskal-Wallis p is the session's existing test (not recomputed).

environment.provider_note: MOCK provider: deterministic heuristic, not a language model — not a measurement

gpu_health.rule: A model's run is flagged when the driver reported a thermal, hardware or power-brake slowdown in more than 5% of the samples, the median SM clock was under 80% of the maximum, the GPU reached 85 °C, or other processes held GPU memory. Hitting the power limit alone (power cap) is normal under load and is only reported. A flagged run's latency and energy may reflect the GPU's state, not the model.

markers.method: Flow starts are recorded by the worker between flows (outside every timed call); each agent's turn is placed from the flow start by adding the wall times of the agents before it.

latency_distribution.warmup_rule: median of the first 5 flows vs the rest; flagged above 1.2x

latency_trend.method: Rolling median over ~10% of the flows (odd window, at least 3). Drift: Spearman rank correlation of flow order vs latency after the first 5 flows (warm-up is checked separately); called a trend when p < 0.05 and the last-quarter median differs from the first-quarter median by more than 10%.
latency_trend.metric: end-to-end latency per flow (s), in run order

notes.total: Total peak = loaded weights + working memory: the larger of torch's peak reserved memory over all agent calls and the NVML device-used peak sampled during the model's run (which also counts the CUDA context). Weights = torch allocated right after load. The decision helper's VRAM limit uses the total peak.
notes.working: Working VRAM (excludes model weights) = the torch allocator peak ABOVE the memory held before each agent call; the mean and the highest over all calls.

notes.normalisation_formula: benefit (accuracy): norm = clamp(value / target, 0, 1); cost (latency, vram, tokens): norm = clamp(target / value, 0, 1)
notes.tokens_definition: tokens = mean over scenarios of the per-scenario TOTAL tokens = mean_scenario( sum over the 4 agents of (input_tokens + output_tokens) ). Config scoring.targets.tokens_total is 'input+output per scenario' — matches; used as-is.
notes.vram_per_agent_note: vram_delta (per-agent) is MARGINAL working memory above the fresh-context baseline and EXCLUDES model weights (per-process isolation baseline).
notes.vram_saw_criterion: SAW VRAM criterion = MARGINAL working memory (mean scenario_peak_vram_mb); no --model-vram supplied. Config target 16000 MB / weight 0.20.

definitions.format: the decide agent's reply is exactly one allowed label (else AgentMeter had to clean it up)
definitions.mitre: the verdict agent names an ATT&CK technique (T####); consistent = the same technique for the same label; reference map = the configured technique for that label
definitions.reference_agreement: share of answers equal to the data set's reference label — a check that the output is meaningful, not a detection score; AgentMeter does not rank detectors
definitions.truncated: at least one agent stopped at its output-token budget (its text may be cut short)
definitions.valid: the decide agent's reply is one of the allowed labels and no agent returned an empty answer
definitions.verdict_consistency: the act agent names the same class as the decide agent

per_class.note: RESOURCE cost per attack class (not detection quality). latency = scenario_total_time_s; vram = mean scenario_peak_vram_mb (MARGINAL working memory, excludes weights); tokens = per-scenario input+output summed over the 4 agents. accuracy is a plain secondary field (mean of the stored `correct` flag), never a ranking. Grouped by the scenario's true class (scenario_results.held_out_label). No classes are invented; empty (model, class) cells report n=0 with null stats.

prompt_composition.note: Each part counted with the model's own tokenizer, separately: parts may not add up exactly. Cacheable = the system prompt's share of input tokens (the same text opens every call of an agent), an upper bound for what prefix caching could skip.

provenance.note: USER/CUSTOM RUN — NOT the validated baseline. These numbers are exploratory (resource efficiency only); they do not change the locked SAW ranking or statistics and must not be merged into them.

rank_stability.method: Paired bootstrap: 500 resamples of the 20 flows (with replacement, the same flows for every model, seed 46); each resample's efficiency-only SAW uses the stored targets and weights. A tie at the top splits the count. p_lowest: share of resamples where the model has the lowest mean of that metric.
rank_stability.note: The absolute SAW clamps at the study targets: models that all beat a target score the same on it, so the top can tie in many resamples even when one model is faster (see p_lowest).

notes.context: Triage quality is context for the efficiency results. It does not change the efficiency score or the ranking.
notes.cost: Cost (energy) per attack caught = the model's cost (energy) for all its flows divided by the attacks it did not dismiss. Measured runs only.
notes.false_escalation: False escalations = benign flows whose predicted class maps to Escalate: analyst time spent on nothing.
notes.flows: The flows are network flows, not IDS alerts: this is flow triage.
notes.gate: A model is recommended for triage only if it meets every gate limit; a check that needs labels is "not checked" on unlabelled input. The gate never changes the efficiency score or the ranking.
notes.missed: Missed attacks = flows whose true class is an attack but whose predicted class maps to Dismiss: the costliest triage error.
notes.policy: The priority comes from this table (the SOC's policy), never from the model: the model classifies the flow, the table says what an analyst does with that class. A class the table does not name, or an answer that could not be parsed, goes to Investigate.
notes.severity: Severity = the default priority of the Snort/Suricata classtype mapped to the predicted class (MITRE ATT&CK has no severity, and flows carry no CVE). "None" = an answer that is not a class.

triage.severity_source: Snort/Suricata classification.config default priorities (1 = High, 2 = Medium, 3 = Low) of the classtype mapped to each class
